subject: Next steps: surge priming & queue model for burst SLOs
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Lee <engops@brightmart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Sep 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: surge priming & queue model for burst SLOs

Evan – great to meet the Platform team earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can align on the SLOs and a joint test plan.

Call highlights (from Redwood):
- Target SLOs you mentioned: p95 inference latency <= 300ms; p99 <= 600ms under normal load. For interactive streaming flows you want first-token latency under 100ms.
- Baseline throughput: ~250 req/s; burst sizing: target up to ~2,000 req/s for 8–15 minute spikes.
- Concurrency: sustained ~400 concurrent streams, momentary spikes to ~1,800 concurrent connections.
- Streaming behavior: token-level streaming required (partial payloads to UI as tokens arrive); need consistent first-token latency.

Operational constraints we discussed:
- Warm pool approach preferred to hit short spike targets (avoid cold GPU startup penalties).
- Cold-starts measured by you were ~70–120s; warm pool activation ideally <15s.
- Queueing: prefer short soft-queue (max 2k in-flight backlog) with graceful fallback to lower-cost model variant when latency degrades.

Immediate ask / next steps (proposal):
1) Redwood and BrightMart run a joint spike test Wed 2028-09-21 10:00 PT (we can shift if needed).
2) BrightMart to share a representative traffic trace (we discussed synthetic CSV) and any observed token counts per request.
3) Redwood to propose warm-pool sizing and a queue model that maps to SLO exposure (we'll include estimations for p95/p99 impact).
4) Exchange a mutual action plan so procurement can approve the temporary capacity needed for the test.

Attachments: priming-sizing.pdf (initial sizing notes) — I'll circulate a more detailed mutual action plan after Marissa and I finalize sizing. Also included a template for the joint test scenario.

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: priming-sizing.pdf]

Thanks Mateo — this is a helpful summary. A couple clarifications from our side before the joint test:

- First-token latency: our UX team says anything above ~100ms for first token on the browser feels sluggish. Can Redwood meet ~50–100ms first-token for the streaming endpoint if warm instances are available?
- Queue behavior: during an internal run last month we saw a backlog build within ~40s when traffic doubled; we need to understand whether Redwood's queueing will buffer or drop requests under extreme duress.
- For the joint test we'll attach a CSV with our synthetic spike (brief summary below) — attaching full CSV in next email.

Brief numbers from our side (headlines):
- Average tokens per request (production samples): 120 tokens
- Median response token count: 140 tokens
- Our simulated spike: ramp 250 -> 2,000 req/s over 30s, hold 10m, drop over 30s.

If Redwood can share an initial warm-pool count recommendation we can provision temporary capacity on our cloud side and check procurement. Attached: burst-sim-results.csv (we'll send the full artifact in the follow-up).

—Evan

EngOps | BrightMart

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Next steps: surge priming & queue model for burst SLOs

Evan — adding a few sizing notes from the runtime team and a recommended test runbook. Quick math first (ballpark):

Assumptions
- Model A (your suggested open model) throughput per GPU: ~120 tokens/sec for 16k context optimized kernel (varies by sequence length).
- Average tokens per request: 120 tokens (your number).
- Effective requests/sec per GPU: ~120 tokens/sec ÷ 120 tokens/req = ~1 req/sec per GPU for synchronous long outputs — but streaming and batching change this (continuous batching increases concurrency utilization).

Warm-pool sizing (proposal)
- To hit ~2,000 req/s peak using pure GPU instances with batching we'd need unrealistic dedicated GPUs; instead we recommend hybrid strategy:
  - Pre-warm 50 inference workers (these are kept with model loaded and KV cache primed) to immediately absorb the first surge; each worker with continuous batching can cover variable throughput depending on batching window.
  - Autoscale policy to add more workers over 20–45s; expected warmup-to-capacity window ~8–12s for warm pool activation, full scale-out to target capacity in ~45–90s depending on backend provisioning.

Queue model recommendation
- Soft queue threshold: allow queue up to 2,000 inflight requests with strict per-request soft-timeout of 12s to avoid long tail latency explosions.
- Fallback policy: when p95 predicted > 450ms, route new traffic to smaller cheaper model variant (quantized) or return fast 503 + retry header to client with recommended backoff.

Test runbook (proposed Wed 2028-09-21 10:00 PT)
- Step 0: Confirm test authorization (procurement) for temporary burst capacity.
- Step 1: Redwood loads the exact trace you provide and primes the KV cache using a 30-minute ramp before spike window.
- Step 2: Execute spike trace while we monitor p50/p95/p99, first-token latency, queue depth, and per-instance CPU/GPU utilization.
- Step 3: If we hit p99 regressions, run fallback to quantized model and measure behavior.

I'll attach a short PDF with the sizing table and we can refine after we see your trace. If Wed doesn't work, propose Thu morning.

Marissa Cole
Sr Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: priming-sizing.pdf]

From: Evan Lee <engops@brightmart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Sep 2028 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: surge priming & queue model for burst SLOs

Marissa — thanks for the detailed sizing notes. We've run a dry spike this morning and attaching the extended CSV. Quick observations from our run:

- When traffic doubled unexpectedly we observed queue build-up after ~40s; p95 climbed to ~1.3s and p99 to ~2.9s before we manually throttled.
- First-token medians are ~120ms on warm instances; on cold starts first-token was double (~240ms).
- We can provision temporary capacity for Wed, but procurement needs a signed mutual action plan for the temporary spend.

Attaching: burst-sim-results-extended.csv (full trace). Two asks for Redwood before Wed:
1) Confirm whether Redwood's soft-queue approach will buffer or start shedding and how it signals clients.
2) Confirm the warm-pool activation path and expected first-token latency when warm pool is used (numbers you shared are helpful but we need a short SLA statement we can show procurement).

Thanks — Evan
[Attachment: burst-sim-results-extended.csv]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Lee <engops@brightmart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Sep 2028 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: surge priming & queue model for burst SLOs

Evan — thanks for the test artifacts and notes. Attached is the mutual action plan for procurement detailing temporary capacity, test window, and acceptance criteria. High level:

- Queueing behavior: Redwood will soft-buffer up to configured backlog (we recommend 2k). When backlog exceeds configured thresholds we will begin graceful shedding with 503 + Retry-After and an automatic routing to a quantized fallback model for non-critical calls. This is the expected behavior and we will instrument metrics and headers so your app can surface retry/backoff to end-users.
- Warm-pool SLA note (for test): if pre-warmed workers are provisioned and KV primed, first-token median during spike is expected in the 50–110ms range; cold starts can be 70–120s to warm full GPU and yield first-token ~200–300ms during initial phase. We'll mark the warm-pool SLA as informational for procurement.

Planned runbook for Wed 10:00 PT (confirm):
- 09:30 PT: Redwood primes KV cache with short pre-load.
- 10:00 PT: Spike window begins (your trace).
- 10:00–10:12 PT: Monitor and collect metrics; Redwood will enforce soft-queue (2k) and apply fallback policy if p95 > 450ms.
- 10:20 PT: Post-run debrief.

Attached: MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx (please have procurement sign). Also cc'ing Ben to coordinate billing approvals if needed.

If you confirm meeting time and procurement sign-off we will provision the warm pool tonight so it's available for the test.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
